# beowulf-fitt-40 — reviewer, pass 1 and pass 2

Method: units edited only through unit-text.json, then `cut_t.py` regenerated units.json; `t` and `ln` verified unchanged for all 21 units. Sources used: Klaeber's text and apparatus (packet), the published parts (grep of beowulf-*.json), grammar. No modern translation opened or recalled. No lexicon was reachable from the sandbox, so lexical claims rest on Klaeber's apparatus and the published parts' own glosses.

Severity: high = wrong grammar, identity or sense; medium = misleading, inconsistent with a published part, or note contradicting its own text; low = wording and precision.

## Findings considered and refused

- 2892 subject of ‘Heht’: Wīglāf kept. The text names no one; the speech just ended is Wīglāf’s and the order follows at once. The note already calls it an inference.
- 2898 ‘sē ðe næs gerād’: kept as “he who rode the headland” (‘næs’ accusative of ‘næs’, ‘gerād’ preterite of ‘gerīdan’); a guess, said so; the ‘ne wæs’ alternative is already named. The speaker is the messenger.
- 2909 ‘higemǣðum’: Klaeber’s word kept with ‘reverence’ as a flagged guess. Rendering from ‘-mēðe’ would make it modify Wīglāf, but Klaeber’s text has the dative plural.
- 2921 ‘Merewīoingas milts ungyfeðe’: ‘milts’ subject, ‘ungyfeðe’ predicate adjective, ‘ūs’ dative; kept. Grammar of ‘-as’ now said plainly (change 13).
- 2926–29 subject: Geats subject, Swedes object, kept. Endings cannot decide (both nominative/accusative plural); ‘ondslyht’ (Ongentheow’s reply, 2929) and ‘ealdre besnyðede Hæðcen’ (2924–25) fit the Geats striking first. Said to be a guess.
- 2930 ‘ābrēot brimwīsan’: Hæthcyn, the Geatish king. Verified from the grammar: it is an accusative singular, Ongentheow is the subject, and the Geatish king is the only leader the passage has named on the Geats’ side who was killed by him. The ‘i’ “leader of the seafarers” kept.
- 2930 ‘gomela’ nominative (Ongentheow) kept; the emended ‘gomelan’ would agree with the woman.
- 2935 Hrefnesholt = Hrefnawudu: kept as already marked a guess.
- 2940 ‘gētan’ “kill” with ‘i’ “cut them down”: kept; flagged guess, and ‘hang some on the gallows-trees’ follows ‘galgtrēowu[m]’, and the note says the picture rests on the additions.
- 2941 ‘i’ opening “But”: asyndeton in the Old English, but the contrast with the night’s threats is real; kept.
- 2943 ‘se gōda’ = Higelac: kept as flagged. ‘i’ “good king” adds “king”, which is true of Higelac and sits in the ‘i’ layer only.
- 2911 alternatives such as ‘undern’ (“morning”): not adopted; no lexicon was reachable to check the form, so ‘underne’ is left a flagged guess. This unit should go to QUESTIONS.md with the other cruces.
- 2919 ‘ealdor dugoðe’: dative kept; ‘l’/‘i’ agree.
- Consistency with published parts: ‘āglǣca’ “awesome one”, ‘wyrm’ “worm”/“dragon”, ‘earfoðlīce’ “hard-wise”, ‘fēðan’ “foot-troop”, ‘Hetware’ (a Frankish people), ‘Hūgas’ (Franks), ‘genǣgan’ “assail”, ‘ferhðgenīðla’ “life-enemy”, Hæthcyn spelling — all agree. No house-rendering conflicts remaining.
- Remembered English in ‘i’: no phrase found that sounds like a famous translation; “keeper”-type formulas absent; ‘the last day of the man they loved’, ‘heavy at heart’ are plain.

## Counts

Changes: 22 (high 3, medium 6, low 13). Findings refused or kept as flagged guesses: 15. Pass 2 re-read all 21 units after the edits and found nothing further beyond the wording in changes already listed; `t` and `ln` verified identical to the drafter’s for every unit.

## Pass 2 (second reviewer) — changes and refusals

Method: re-read all 21 units against the Old English and the apparatus (labels, `l` word by word, `l`↔`i`, remembered English, published parts); checked every `gloss.json` parse against its line(s). Text edits through unit-text.json and cut_t.py (only unit 2910’s note changed; `t` and `ln` verified identical for all 21 units). Build not run.

### Text changes

23. 2910 · n · medium · pass 1’s ‘underne’ = ‘undyrne’ (‘openly’) was stated with too little support: the note only said it could not find ‘underne’, then adopted ‘undyrne’. · The base word ‘undyrne’ ‘not hidden’ is supported by the published part at 409; ‘underne’ for it is not found in any source reachable, so the note now says plainly that ‘openly’ is a guess and offers the alternative, the manuscript’s ‘under’ with the dative (‘among Franks and Frisians’), whose sense is much the same. `l` “openly” and `i` “openly known” kept, so `l`/`i`/note agree.

### Gloss changes (gloss.json)

G1. besnyðede · medium · lemma ‘besnyððan’ disagreed with the note’s ‘besnyðian’ and ‘weak verb’ was unspecific · ‘besnyðian … weak verb II’.
G2. merewīoingas · high · parsed as “genitive, dependent on milts”, but the form’s ‘-as’ is not genitive (the unit note says so) · now: masculine plural, ending nominative/accusative, construction with ‘milts’ irregular and uncertain.
G3. gūð-scilfingas · medium · “nominative” only; the unit reads it as the accusative object · “nominative or accusative”.
G4. sinherge · medium · “accusative singular” though ‘-ge’ is the dative ending of ‘here’ · case stated as uncertain.
G5. underne · medium · made to match the revised unit note (guess; alternative ‘under’).
G6. gētan · low · ‘Thorkelin proposed grētan’ is wrong: the apparatus gives Thorpe and Sedgefield; ‘perhaps from gȳtan’ unsupported · corrected, speculation dropped.
G7. hagan · low · “probably a fortified spot” against the note’s ‘enclosure’ · “enclosure, hedged place”.
G8. hrefnawudu · low · “accusative singular after wið” — ‘wið’ takes either case and the form does not decide · “accusative or dative”.
G9. ecgclif · low · “sea-cliff” asserted for ‘ecgclif’; ‘ēgclif’ is only a reading, ‘water-cliff’ · reworded.
G10. dugoðe · low · parse omitted that the form is also genitive singular (the unit note discusses both readings) · added.
G11. heaðoweorc · low · “here the tidings” pinned to a line · reworded without ‘here’.
G12. ungyfeðe · low · stray comma · removed.
G13. __broaden__ feorhgenīðlan · medium · added reading “dative singular or accusative plural” contradicted the unit note (accusative plural) · now “accusative plural; or a collective dative singular”; old entry whole.
G14. __broaden__ berofene, næs, sume · low · added readings shortened (result near 260); næs and sume marked as guesses; old entries whole.

### Pass 2 findings considered and refused

- Units 2892–2945 otherwise: every label, `l` and `i` re-checked; no further error found. ‘ondlonge’, ‘ǣrdæge’, ‘dugoðe’ at 2945 (dative of company), ‘lēoda’ genitive, ‘wēne’ first person, ‘oðēodon’/‘geēodon’ plural preterites: true as labelled.
- ‘undern’ ‘morning’ for ‘underne’: not offered; it does not fit the clause and no support found.
- Published-part consistency (‘elne gegongen’ 893, ‘genǣg’ 2204, ‘on fēðan’ 2497, ‘undyrne’ 409): confirmed.
- Known-form entries all cover their use here; no further __broaden__ needed. Novel forms: all 82 present in gloss.json, none extra.

Counts (pass 2): text 1 (medium 1); gloss 14 (high 1, medium 5, low 8).
